solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Caper has loveless gang brought into prison

indicators.note: love is the zero-shaped letter, so a loveless word has that letter taken out
something brought into a building ends up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a gang of criminals is a mob

explanation.surface: A prank sees a gang locked up, with the love gone out of their lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scores, which crosswords take as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambol is a playful leap, the same sense as caper used as a noun for a frisky skip.

clue.text: Access in A&E beautiful woman almost blocks

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
something that blocks a passage sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: Venus, goddess of beauty, stands for any beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman is blocking the way into the hospital's emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department. VENUS loses its last letter and sits between A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way in, as in an avenue of approach, so it means a route of access.

clue.text: Count supporting relatives: claret here in store?

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: one's blood is one's family, as in blood relatives
to bank on is to count on

explanation.surface: A count props up his family in a vault full of claret wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts BANK beneath BLOOD. Claret is slang for blood, the sense the definition plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood bank stores donated blood, and claret is slang for blood, so it is where claret is kept.

clue.text: Patriarch and prophet beheaded sea-monster

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: Levi, son of Jacob, founder of a tribe of Israel
Nathan, the prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: Two biblical figures, one losing his head, set against a sea-monster.
explanation.walkthrough: NATHAN without its first letter gives ATHAN, appended to LEVI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is the huge sea creature of the Old Testament, so a sea-monster by name.

clue.text: How 21 may announce breaks for Holland gin?

indicators.note: announcing is speaking out, and a drunk's speech is slurred, so the word is taken by its slurred sound

blocks.note: snaps means breaks; slurred by a drunk it becomes shnaps

explanation.surface: A question about how a drinker might call out for a Dutch gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is BOOZER, a drunk, whose slurred 's' turns SNAPS into a sound like SCHNAPPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, and the term has been used for Dutch gin distilled at Schiedam.

clue.text: Sweet and virtuous person with uncouth student

explanation.surface: A pleasant, good person keeps company with a boorish student.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a pastry dessert, and sweet is the British word for a dessert course.

clue.text: Mrs Ogden perhaps regularly thrilled American

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A soap character is said to be thrilled by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilda Ogden was a long-running character in the British TV soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilda is the first name of Mrs Ogden; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of a Hilda.

clue.text: Eliot's cruellest month lands pair in trouble

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A poet's harsh month gets a couple into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land opens 'April is the cruellest month'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous opening line of The Waste Land names this month as the cruellest, so the quotation identifies it.

clue.text: Princes out to consume hot dog

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
consuming takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Royals step out to eat a hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'hot dog' a snack; 'hot' is H and 'dog' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinscher is a breed of dog, as in the Dobermann pinscher, so this is an example.

clue.text: Top Gun

blocks.note: first meaning: a spinning top is something that turns round and round
second meaning: a handgun with a rotating cylinder

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Top Gun' is the film; split, each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's top is a thing that spins on its axis, and a pistol with a rotating chamber is called by the same name.

clue.text: A source of roar in wild feline?

definitions.text: A source of roar in wild feline?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is kept
in places the first pieces inside the next one

blocks.note: the lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A question about where a big cat's roar comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go inside LYNX, and the whole clue also describes the answer: the voice box is where a wild cat's roar is produced.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box in the throat, which produces any animal's roar.

clue.text: Plain fish containing bones

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: bones is slang for a doctor, abbreviated DR

explanation.surface: A simple fish dish with the bones left in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' (from sawbones) is old slang for a doctor, hence DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless flat land of the Arctic, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Lifeless hair — no resolution available here

explanation.surface: Limp, dull hair that no treatment can fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill in a dispute where neither side can reach a settlement.

clue.text: Record cut in the infernal world

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A recording is made in hell.
explanation.walkthrough: DISC loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and, in Dante, the name of the city of hell.

clue.text: Vulnerability's shivering in ocean around bank

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a ship heels when it banks or tilts over

explanation.surface: A weak spot shows as someone shivers in the sea near the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA reversed is AES; CHILL goes inside it, then HEEL follows. 's here stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was invulnerable except at his heel, so the phrase means a single fatal weakness.

clue.text: Syphilis rampant on the way in alien world

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up, and in a down clue rising means read from the bottom upward
in places the first pieces inside the next

blocks.note: the pox is a slang term for syphilis

explanation.surface: A disease runs riot on its way into a strange planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien world' looks like the whole definition, but 'alien' is wordplay for the outer letters; 'world' alone defines. The pox is old slang for syphilis.
explanation.definitionFit: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun, so another world.

clue.text: Henry II welcoming to second son in stinking pants?

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the next pieces go inside

blocks.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry
the Roman numeral taken as letters

explanation.surface: A king takes in his younger son, whose trousers smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral II splits around the inserted pieces. 'Pants' in the definition is a verb, breathes hard, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is bad breath, and pants are gasping breaths, so foul-smelling pants are halitosis.

clue.text: Swede in furrow by a secure area

blocks.note: to bag is to secure or get hold of

explanation.surface: A Swedish person stands in a ploughed groove beside a fenced-off zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a person from Sweden; it is the root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutabaga is the American name for the root vegetable the British call a swede.

clue.text: Seat that punishes French duke, monarch's minion

blocks.note: a tool is someone used by another

explanation.surface: A seat of punishment for a French nobleman who serves a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducking-stool was a chair on a pole used to plunge offenders into water as punishment.

clue.text: Murder across the pond that is cold-hearted?

indicators.note: a word with something at its heart has it placed in its middle

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A question about whether an American killing was done in cold blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' means in America; ice is US slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang to ice someone is to kill them, so it is murder in US speech.

clue.text: Opener in theatre succeeded, training in style

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: call in the sense of a manner of address or name

explanation.surface: A first-night show in the theatre was a hit, with drilled style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener in theatre' suggests a first night; the theatre is the operating theatre and the opener a surgical knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the blade a surgeon uses to open up a patient in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Touring Australia old South African drunkard …

indicators.note: touring a country means going round it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the Boers were Dutch settlers in South Africa
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A veteran South African tours Australia and drinks heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is also British slang for a pub; here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is a heavy drinker, from booze meaning alcohol.

clue.text: Everyone for cessation in bitter feud in city

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one word swaps in where another stood

blocks.note: a vendetta is a bitter feud

explanation.surface: Everyone wants the bitter feud in the city to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: In VENDETTA the END is swapped for ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital city of Malta.

clue.text: … gets round in?

blocks.note: surface reading, continuing from 21: the drunk buys a round of drinks at the bar
setter's reading: the round is a bullet put into a gun's chamber

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 21, so the drunkard seems to be buying drinks; Neo confirmed the round is a bullet, and the verb describes arming a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To put ammunition into a firearm is to charge it, so someone doing that with a cartridge is arming the weapon.

clue.text: Country knight introduced to rustic goat

indicators.note: rustic means rough and unrefined, so the letters come out roughly rearranged
being introduced to something brings it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A nation where a knight meets a farmyard goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom, a country.

clue.text: Calcium should be removed from spot preparation

indicators.note: removing something from a word takes those letters out

blocks.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: Advice that calcium should be kept out of a spot cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot preparation' reads as a pimple cream, but spot is LOCATION and preparation alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid preparation applied to the skin.

clue.text: Officer leaving Trudeau for one in Promised Land

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: DI, Detective Inspector, a police officer
Justin Trudeau, former Canadian prime minister

explanation.surface: An official quits the Trudeau camp to reach the Promised Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaan is the land God promised to Abraham's descendants in the Bible.

clue.text: Fashionable zip set in lines for pocket?

indicators.note: fashioning something shapes it anew, so these letters are reworked
lining something sits inside it, so the word goes within the other piece

explanation.surface: A smart set of zips sewn into the lining of a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' looks like IN, but it is the anagram signal; the word in comes from the clue as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Pint-size means small, the same sense as pocket used as an adjective, as in a pocket edition.

clue.text: Building after war — who advocated that?

definitions.text: Building after war — who advocated that?

explanation.surface: A question about who argued for reconstruction after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: George Marshall's Marshall Plan funded rebuilding Europe after the Second World War, so the whole clue also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: US Secretary of State George Marshall proposed the Marshall Plan for European post-war recovery.

clue.text: Stares awkwardly? These are stunners!

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: People gawp at something gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunners' suggests beautiful people; it means stun guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, a device that stuns its target.
